old: Pencroff took the lad by the arm. They waded, ran, waded again.
new: They waded, ran, waded again. But the ebb had scoured the sands into hollows that ran down toward the gut, and in one of these the bottom went from under Herbert's feet. The current took him, turned him over, and drew him seaward. Pencroff threw himself after him, caught him by the collar, lost him, caught him again by the arm, and, planting himself against the stream, hauled him up on firmer sand. Then he took the lad under the shoulder, and carried rather than led him.

old: Glass! I have put into a good many ports, my boy, and I never saw the like.
new: Glass! I have put in at many good ports, my boy, and I have never seen the like.¶The sailor might well say so.¶Only in late years had the fishermen of the north of Europe, in the cod fisheries of Norway, begun to buoy their great nets with globes of blown glass, which do not drink the water as cork does, and neither rot nor sink. They were still a novelty of the northern seas, and an American sailor had very likely never seen one.¶That such a float should lie upon Lincoln Island would astonish no one who knows the roads which the sea opens to floating bodies. In the South Pacific the waters turn in a great round: up the coasts of Chile and Peru, westward below the line, then south, and back to the east under the westerly winds; and whatever falls into that round, a spar, a cask, a float, it carries for months and for years. The sea is patient, and sooner or later it brings in everything that it does not sink.

old: He did not. The sea had uncovered the thing once; it might give back something else at the next low water, the net, or some piece of what had been on the bar. The sailor meant to go back and see, and to bring home with his own hands whatever he found, and lay it on the table before them all.
new: He did not. He meant to tell it, he had promised it; but the rest could not be told by halves. To speak of the float was to speak of the bar, of the hour of low water let slip, of the flood which he, a seaman, had not watched, and of the lad turned over in the current like a piece of weed. He had let the boy stay out on the bar with the flood making, against a rule he had kept all his life.

old: We had it, Pencroff, said Herbert. "For an hour."
The sailor looked at him, and answered nothing; then they went back across the sand to the lines.
new: Then he shook himself, as Top does coming out of the water. "Bah!" he cried. "The sea has taken, and the sea will give us something else. She owes us that much, my boy." And he put his great hand on the lad's shoulder, and they went back across the sand to the lines.
